claims.statement: A Claim is one atomic factual proposition identified by a stable OpenWiki-generated id, carrying a statement and one or more Evidence records, where each Evidence pairs a resolver-owned resource identity with an opaque version token captured when the Claim was established.

The code brain splits Claims responsibilities into a persistence store (ClaimsStore), run-scoped working state (ClaimSession), and a runtime that wires them together and exposes a single finalize entrypoint.

Claim state persists as JSON sidecars under the wiki directory's .claims folder (openwiki/.claims/ for a repository), mirroring each grounded page's path below the wiki prefix with a .json extension; ClaimsStore and the path helpers take the wiki's virtual page prefix as a parameter, defaulting to /openwiki/.
A page sidecar records the schema version, a sha256 pageVersion hash of the generated Markdown bytes, the complete claims array, and an optional durable verification event.
Only pages that own factual state are grounded: reserved files (index.md, log.md, instructions.md) and anything inside the .claims directory are excluded from Claim persistence.
Sidecars are written atomically by serializing validated state to a temporary file and renaming it into place, removing the temporary file on failure so a partial write cannot corrupt a sidecar.
Evidence is addressed by a canonical repo:// URI whose fragment is an optional GitHub-style inclusive line range, and a single-line fragment such as #L8 is canonicalized to #L8-L8.
Repository evidence parsing rejects paths that escape the repository, absolute or drive-letter paths, control characters, and any reference to .git metadata or generated openwiki output.
Evidence resolution is deterministic and model-free, reading files through a containment gate that refuses symbolic links and filesystem aliases before producing a version.
Evidence versions are content-derived SHA-256 tokens: whole-file evidence uses repo-file-v1 over the entire file, so a version mismatch is exactly a content change.

Line-range evidence versions embed resolver-owned relocation anchors so that when edits move or resize a range the resolver can locate the same selected text and keep the version stable when the content did not actually change.
Resolution returns null when a file or range no longer exists, which is distinct from a resource that resolves at a changed version.

Preflight classifies each persisted Claim by re-resolving its evidence against the recorded prior version, marking a Claim unresolved when any resource no longer resolves and stale when a resource resolves at a different version, with unresolved taking precedence; an EvidenceSecurityError (symbolic-link or filesystem-alias containment refusal) is caught and treated as unresolved for that resource rather than aborting the run.

Preflight freshness checks do not create mandatory agent work and propagate resolution errors so they cannot be mistaken for deleted evidence, with the single exception of EvidenceSecurityError, which is caught and reported as an unresolved issue for reconciliation rather than aborting the update.

Applying claim operations is an all-or-nothing transaction that validates every operation and resolves all evidence before any state is mutated, rejecting batches that target an id twice, reference unknown ids, or repeat or duplicate an evidence resource.
A confirm re-resolves a Claim's existing evidence to refresh its versions, and an update that omits evidence likewise retains and refreshes the current resources.
Claim identifiers are globally unique across pages: the session allocates collision-free ids and rejects a page whose state would claim an id already owned by another page.

Applying a successful mutation marks only the owning page dirty and clears the grounding issues for the Claim ids the batch targeted, so reconciling a stale or unresolved Claim removes its evidence debt.
Inspecting a page is side-effect-free: it returns cloned model-facing Claims with opaque evidence versions stripped and any preflight issue attached, without creating a write obligation.
Finalization is the durability boundary that persists only changed pages and refuses a page that still has unresolved evidence debt.
Before writing a sidecar, finalization re-resolves every Claim's evidence a final time and refuses to persist the page if any resource disappeared or changed version since the mutation was accepted.
Finalization removes orphaned sidecars whose pages no longer exist, deletes sidecars for pages whose Markdown vanished during the run, and removes sidecars for pages recorded as deleted.

Each page's Markdown is hashed before its sidecar is written so the persisted pageVersion describes the exact bytes on disk, and a page with a non-empty Claim set receives a durable verification event while a fully retracted page is persisted without one.
Per-page finalization failures are isolated as warnings rather than aborting the run, but the runtime treats any accumulated warning as a durability failure and rejects.

Durable Claims evidence is projected into OKF sources front matter, collapsing precise line ranges to whole-file repo:// resources, assigning OpenWiki-owned entries deterministic ids derived from the resource, and retaining independently authored producer sources.

Durable verification is projected into the OKF verified field by retaining all producer-authored events whose by actor is not in the openwiki/<version> family, then appending at most one active durable Claims verification event per page (or none when ineligible), normalizing bare mappings to canonical list form, and recording pre-projection Markdown so a failed hash refresh can roll the field back.
Only a page that is persisted, clean, non-empty, free of evidence debt, and carrying a verification event is eligible for a machine verification stamp.

Because OKF projection can rewrite code-owned front matter and change page bytes, the runtime re-hashes represented pages after projection and rolls back a newly exposed verification stamp when its page hash cannot be refreshed, so a stamp never outlives an accurate pageVersion.

The Claims runtime is prepared only for repository output outside chat mode, starting a fresh init from empty state while still discovering existing sidecars as orphan candidates and running full preflight for updates and resumed inits.

The repository evidence resolver is configured with the repository root and the shared .openwikiignore read-boundary rules, so evidence resolution honors the same path exclusions as the agent's file reads.
Each processing phase wraps the resolver with a fresh evidence cache so every resource and prior-version pair resolves at most once within that phase without caching across a freshness boundary.

finalize accepts an excludedPages set of pages whose jobs were skipped during an interrupted run and leaves them untouched, skipping their persistence, evidence recheck, and sidecar deletion; finishRepositoryRun validates that every skipped job carries its original page snapshot, derives skippedPages from the skipped jobs, and passes the set both to finalize and to the post-run durability assertion so skipped pages are exempt from Claims persistence and the no-orphan/durable-page checks.

At submit_page the run grounds each page individually before advancing the queue: submitRepositoryPage runs page-local validation and front-matter repair without the run mutation lock, then takes the lock to run reconcilePageClaims (translating the sparse proposed Claim decisions into a complete confirm/update/add/retract operation batch), then claimsRuntime.finalize (excluding every other still-pending page so a concurrent worker's transient bytes are not projected), then assertPageClaimsDurable, which reloads the freshly written sidecar and proves the page durable before the job is marked complete.

assertPageClaimsDurable is the strict per-page proof that refuses the page when the sidecar was not persisted, its pageVersion hash does not match the current Markdown bytes, it carries no verification event, that event is not durably projected into the front-matter verified field, or the persisted Claim set differs from the session's expected set in count, statement, or evidence resources.

submit_page takes a sparse ProposedPageClaimReconciliation with three optional fields (confirmedClaimIds, claims, retractedClaimIds); reconcilePageClaims confirms existing issue-free Claims omitted from every field automatically, rejects a submission that leaves any issue-bearing Claim without an explicit confirm/update/retract decision, and refuses a result that would leave a completed factual page with zero Claims.

A proposed Claim with an existing id that is unchanged folds into a confirm and a changed one becomes a partial update carrying only the differing fields; a proposed Claim without an id is matched against an existing identical Claim before falling back to an add. Retraction is delete-like across retries: an unknown id in retractedClaimIds is tolerated when no longer owned, while unknown update/confirm ids remain strict.

nextRepositoryPage returns the first pending job not excluded by the caller's in-flight worker set without reserving or mutating it, along with its existingClaimCount and claimsRequiringAttention (only Claims carrying a stale or unresolved issue); issue-free Claims are summarized as a count rather than enumerated, so focused updates need not carry them.

inspectRepositoryPageClaims (the openwiki_inspect_page_claims tool) returns the current pending page's complete compact Claim set without opaque evidence versions, and only for the current pending job; it is the on-demand way to obtain complete Claim ids before intentionally revising or removing otherwise-current content whose Claims are not in claimsRequiringAttention.

The model-facing Claims substance and reconciliation standards live as shared constants in src/claims/guidance.ts: CLAIMS_SUBSTANCE_GUIDANCE (the materiality test, atomic-means-one-idea principle, and repo:// evidence-resource form requirement) and CLAIMS_RECONCILIATION_GUIDANCE (the sparse-decision rules). The page-worker prompt (createRepositoryPagePrompt) inlines both constants into the system prompt for every init/update job, while the MCP server INSTRUCTIONS constant inlines only CLAIMS_RECONCILIATION_GUIDANCE alongside workspace-discovery guidance and the deterministic page-job lifecycle, so the reconciliation rules reach every host integration and tool description.

The Claims model applies only to repository code wikis and repository evidence: the evidence resolver is RepositoryEvidenceResolver, rooted at a Git top-level and addressing files with repo:// URIs, with no connector-derived evidence path, so facts sourced from host integrations or connectors are not represented as Claims.

Before a bounded page worker starts model-owned work, captureRepositoryPageSnapshot records the page's pre-run Markdown and its Claims sidecar together; on failure restoreRepositoryPage replays both through the backend and store (writing the captured PageClaims when one existed, or deleting the sidecar otherwise), so a failed attempt cannot leave Markdown and Claims out of sync.

skipRepositoryPage runs the restore under the run mutation lock, rebuilds the entire ClaimsRuntime from durable sidecars via prepareClaimsRuntime so the shared session reflects the rolled-back state, marks the job skipped, and records an interrupted update; because the runtime is rebuilt from disk, a concurrent worker's already-durable completion cannot be lost.

When resolving a line-range evidence resource against a prior version, the resolver prefers an exact content-hash match at the URI's hinted span, then relocation by the first and last selected-line hashes, then relocation between surrounding context hashes; any ambiguity resolves to null (unresolved) rather than guessing.

ClaimsStore is parameterized by the wiki's virtual page prefix (defaulting to /openwiki/): its wiki directory is <rootDir>/openwiki for a repository root or rootDir itself when the prefix is /, and a wiki rooted at its own directory must not be a symbolic link.
